props.gloss_en: [the 1500-city:] if [the nine died] in one day or in four days -- this is not a pestilence
and a city that sends out five hundred foot-soldiers, such as Kfar Amiko, from which three dead go out in three days one after the other -- this is a pestilence
[the 500-city:] in one day or in four days -- this is not a pestilence
Drokart, a city sending out five hundred foot-soldiers, had three dead in one day; Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda decreed a fast
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: according to whom [did you decree]? according to R' Meir
R' Meir: [if an ox] spaced its gorings it is liable [as forewarned]; [if] it brought its gorings close together, all the more so!
Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: let the master arise and come to us
R' Yosei: it is not a person's place that honours him; the person honours his place

for so we find at Mount Sinai: while the Shekhina rested on it the Torah said 'neither let the flocks nor the herds feed before that mount' (Ex 34:3); once it departed, 'when the shofar sounds long they shall come up to the mount' (Ex 19:13)

and so we find with the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness: while it was pitched the Torah said 'that they put out of the camp every leper' (Num 5:2); once the curtains were rolled up, zavim and lepers were permitted to enter there
Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda: if so, let me arise and come to the master
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: better that a maneh son of a peras come to a maneh son of a maneh, and not that a maneh son of a maneh come to a maneh son of a peras
[in Sura there was pestilence, in Rav's neighbourhood none;] they thought it was because of Rav's great merit
rather, because of a certain man who would lend a hoe and a shovel for burial
[in Drokart there was a fire, in Rav Huna's neighbourhood none;] they thought it was through Rav Huna's great merit
rather, because of a certain woman who heats her oven and lends it to her neighbours
they told Rav Yehuda: locusts have come; he decreed a fast
they told Rav Yehuda: there is pestilence among the pigs; he decreed a fast
shall we say Rav Yehuda holds that a plague sent upon one species is sent upon all species?
no: pigs are different, for their intestines resemble those of people
they told Shmuel: there is pestilence in Bei Chozai; he decreed a fast
they told Rav Nachman: there is pestilence in Eretz Yisrael; he decreed a fast, saying: if the lady is struck, is not the maidservant all the more so!
the reason is [that it is] lady and maidservant; but maidservant and maidservant -- no [fast]
it is different there: since there are caravans that travel [between them], it comes along with them
Abba the bloodletter would receive greetings from the heavenly academy every day
and Abaye every Shabbat eve
and Rava every Yom Kippur eve
Abaye was distressed on account of Abba the bloodletter; they told him: you cannot do as he does
when he would let blood, he would place men apart and women apart
he had a garment with a slit at the place of the incision, which he would dress a woman in, so that he would not look at her
he had a hidden place where his fees were thrown: one who had, threw in; one who had not was not shamed
when a young scholar came to him he took no fee, and afterwards gave him coins, saying: go and restore yourself
Abba the bloodletter: I said [to myself], a ransom of captives came the rabbis' way, and they were ashamed to tell me
Abba the bloodletter: from that hour I put them out of my mind for charity
Rava was distressed on account of Abaye; they told him: it is enough for you that you protect the whole city
is there anyone in this market who is a son of the world to come?
Eliyahu: that one [black shoes, no tekhelet thread on his cloak] is a son of the world to come
the man: I am a jailer; I confine the men apart and the women apart and put my bed between them, so they not come to transgression
when I see a Jewish woman on whom gentiles have set their eyes, I risk my life and save her (the betrothed girl and the wine dregs)
[why no tzitzit and black shoes?] I come and go among gentiles, so that they not know I am a Jew
when they make a decree I tell the rabbis, and they pray for mercy and annul the decree
[why 'go now and come tomorrow'?] at that hour they had made a decree, and I said: first I will go and hear it, and send to the rabbis to pray for mercy over it
Eliyahu: these too [the two brothers] are sons of the world to come
the brothers: we are jesters; we cheer the sad
the brothers: when we see two who have a quarrel between them, we take pains and make peace for them
